items.label: section_header
items.text: 15 EXTRACTION AND USES OF METALS

items.label: text
items.text: Metals are some of the most important materials that we use in everyday life. This chapter explores the principles behind the extraction of metals from their ores. We will also look at the properties of alloys and the uses of some metals.

items.label: section_header
items.text: LEARNING OBJECTIVES

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that most metals are extracted from ores found in the Earth's crust and that unreactive metals are often found as the uncombined element

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain how the method of extraction of a metal is related to its position in the reactivity series, illustrated by carbon extraction for iron and electrolysis for aluminium

items.label: list_item
items.text: Be able to comment on a metal extraction process, given appropriate information (detailed knowledge of the processes used in the extraction of a specific metal is not required)

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXTRACTING METALS FROM THEIR ORES

items.label: text
items.text: Most metals are found in the Earth's crust combined with other elements. The individual compounds are called minerals.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 15.1 Pyrite (iron pyrites), FeS2

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 15.2 Magnetite, Fe3O4

items.label: text
items.text: Figures 15.1 and 15.2 show samples of some iron-containing minerals; they are normally found mixed with other unwanted minerals in rocks. An ore is a sample of rock that contains enough of a mineral for it to be worthwhile to extract the metal. Most metals are extracted from ores found in the Earth's crust.

items.label: text
items.text: A few very unreactive metals, such as gold, are found native. That means that they exist naturally as the uncombined element. Silver and copper are also sometimes found native, although much more rarely.

items.label: text
items.text: Many ores contain either oxides or compounds that are easily converted to oxides. Sulfides such as sphalerite (zinc blende), ZnS, can be easily converted into an oxide by heating in air, a process known as roasting.

items.label: section_header
items.text: MINERALS AND ORES

items.label: section_header
items.text: DID YOU KNOW?

items.label: text
items.text: The price of a metal is affected by how common the ore is and how difficult it is to extract the metal from the ore.

items.label: section_header
items.text: HINT

items.label: text
items.text: You do not need to remember the names of these ores/minerals for the exam.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXTRACTING THE METAL

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain the uses of aluminium, copper, iron and steel in terms of their properties (the types of steel will be limited to low-carbon (mild), high-carbon and stainless)

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that an alloy is a mixture of a metal and one or more elements, usually other metals or carbon

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain why alloys are harder than pure metals
